title: Prison Cells After N Days
summary: Given an array representing the initial state of 8 prison cells, where each cell is either occupied (1) or vacant (0), and an integer n, determine the state of the cells after n days following specific transition rules.
statement: Given an array representing the initial state of 8 prison cells, where each cell is either occupied (1) or vacant (0), and an integer n, determine the state of the cells after n days following specific transition rules. The first and last cells cannot have two adjacent neighbors.
constraints: There are exactly eight cells; endpoints become zero each day.
An interior cell becomes one exactly when its two neighbors were equal.
hints: Only 2^6 interior states exist after the first day, so repetition is guaranteed.
Remember each state with remaining days and jump by a detected cycle length.
On repetition reduce n modulo the difference in remaining-day counts.
The transition is deterministic, so revisiting a state repeats the entire future cycle.
editorial: The transition is deterministic, so revisiting a state repeats the entire future cycle.

tests.explanation: Cycle detection reduces the large day count to the repeated state 0,0,1,1,1,1,1,0.
